title: Evaluating expressions with stacks
summary: Reverse Polish notation is evaluated with one operand stack; infix expressions use a stack of partial results and signs.

sections.title: Reverse Polish notation
Infix with + − and parentheses (recognition)
sections.body: Basic Calculator (LeetCode 224): keep `result`, `sign`, and a stack. On '(' push the current result and sign, reset; on ')' pop and combine. With * and / (LeetCode 227): push numbers with their sign, and immediately combine with the top for * and /; sum the stack at the end.

sections.title: Pitfalls
sections.body:
✍️ "-3" is a number, not an operator: check whole-token equality, not the first character.
- Intermediate products can exceed int; use `long long`.
